title: 2013 Marshmallow Twist: Broken Promises Cut Patience by 75%
offcenter_creator_bet: My bet: willpower is mostly self-trust — when payoffs feel rigged, grabbing now is rational. Willpower or trust?

acts.name: The Willpower Myth & 2013 Crayon Twist
sentences: Books claim eating one marshmallow proves weak grit!
Yet one broken promise made kids eat it four times faster!
Psychologists proved it with Celeste Kidd's crayon promise test.
Inside the room, things turned upside down fast.
Late night snacks wreck your clean habit streak.
You blame weak grit right away.
In nineteen seventy-two, Walter Mischel built that famous room.
One white treat sat on a clean plate.
Wait fifteen minutes alone, and you got two.

acts.name: Kept vs Broken Art Promises & 3-Minute Crash
sentences: Half the rooms saw the adult keep her word.
She brought in a full wood tray of pens.
In the other fourteen, like a jury plus two, she lied.

Only then did she put one marshmallow down.

Behind the behavior sits a sharp trust scale.

acts.name: Twelve-Minute Patience & The Brain's Value Scale
